tour.overview:
Lima was founded by Francisco Pizarro in 1535 as the 'City of Kings' and became the capital of the Spanish Viceroyalty of Peru, which governed most of South America. Its historic centre of baroque churches and wooden balconies has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1988. Long before the Spanish, the coast was home to cultures that built adobe pyramids, and today Lima is famous above all for its food: ceviche, Nikkei and Chifa cuisines and some of the world's best restaurants.

This private day shows Lima's history and flavours with a licensed guide and a car. You explore the colonial centre and the catacombs of San Francisco, have a ceviche lunch with a pisco sour lesson, see the pre-Inca pyramid of Huaca Pucllana and end in Barranco at sunset.

AT A GLANCE
• Duration: about 8 hours
• Start and end: your hotel in Lima
• Type: private tour with licensed guide, car and driver
• Booking: on request – we confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay only then
• Level: easy

WHAT YOU SEE
• The Plaza Mayor, the cathedral and the Government Palace.
• The monastery of San Francisco and its catacombs.
• Huaca Pucllana.
• The Miraflores clifftops and the Parque del Amor.
• Barranco.

WHY THIS WORKS
Lima's traffic is heavy; the car and your guide's timing get you between the centre and the coast efficiently.

WHO IT SUITS
Food lovers, history lovers and anyone with a day in Lima before or after Cusco.

WHO MAY PREFER ANOTHER TOUR
If you prefer the desert and the sea, choose our Paracas and Huacachina day trip.

PRACTICAL INFORMATION
The changing of the guard at the Government Palace takes place around noon most days. From June to September, Lima is often covered by a grey sea mist called the garúa.

days.name: The colonial centre, San Francisco and its catacombs, a ceviche lunch, Huaca Pucllana, Miraflores and Barranco
days.description:
What to expect: Lima's colonial heart, its pre-Inca past and its famous food, with a licensed guide, private car, tickets and lunch.

Your guide and driver collect you at your hotel at about 9:00 and drive to the historic centre. In the Plaza Mayor, where Pizarro founded the city, you see the Government Palace, built on the site of his house, the Archbishop's Palace with its carved wooden balconies, and the cathedral, where Pizarro's remains lie in a chapel decorated with mosaics. A few blocks away, the monastery of San Francisco, finished in 1674, has cloisters lined with Sevillian tiles, a library of ancient books and, beneath the church, catacombs where the bones of some 25,000 people are arranged in geometric patterns.

Lunch is at a cevichería, with ceviche – fresh fish cured in lime with chilli, red onion and sweet potato – and other coastal dishes, and a lesson in making a pisco sour, Peru's national cocktail. In the afternoon you visit Huaca Pucllana, a great pyramid of handmade adobe bricks built by the Lima culture between 200 and 700 AD, standing in the middle of the modern district of Miraflores. You walk along the clifftop parks of Miraflores, including the Parque del Amor with its mosaic benches, watching paragliders above the Pacific.

You end in Barranco, the bohemian district of artists and writers, with its colourful mansions, street murals and the wooden Bridge of Sighs, and watch the sunset over the ocean from a café or a terrace. You are back at your hotel at about 17:30.

SCHEDULE (approximate times)
09:00 – Pick-up at your hotel.
09:45 – Plaza Mayor and the cathedral.
11:00 – Monastery of San Francisco and catacombs.
12:30 – Ceviche lunch and pisco sour lesson.
14:30 – Huaca Pucllana.
15:30 – Miraflores clifftops.
16:15 – Barranco and sunset.
17:30 – Back at your hotel.

GOOD TO KNOW
• The Larco Museum, with its pre-Columbian gold and ceramics, can replace Huaca Pucllana.
• Ceviche is traditionally eaten at lunch, when the fish is freshest.
• The Magic Water Circuit fountain show can be added in the evening.

INCLUDED: private car and driver, licensed guide, entrance tickets, lunch with pisco sour lesson, bottled water, hotel pick-up and drop-off.
NOT INCLUDED: extra drinks, tips.

Meals: lunch.

faq.question: How does booking on request work?
faq.answer: You choose a date and the number of travellers and send the request. Nothing is charged. We confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay online only when the tour is confirmed.

faq.question: Are the tickets included?
faq.answer: Yes: the cathedral, San Francisco and Huaca Pucllana.

faq.question: Is lunch included?
faq.answer: Yes, a ceviche lunch with a pisco sour lesson. Non-alcoholic versions and non-fish dishes are available.

faq.question: Is ceviche safe to eat?
faq.answer: Yes, at the reputable cevicherías we use, where the fish is caught the same morning.

faq.question: Is it suitable for children?
faq.answer: Yes. Children find the catacombs fascinating and love the parks. Child seats are provided free of charge on request.

faq.question: Is it suitable for people with limited mobility?
faq.answer: Largely. The catacombs have narrow, low passages and stairs; other sites are accessible.

faq.question: Can we add a cooking class?
faq.answer: Yes. A Peruvian cooking class with a market visit can replace part of the afternoon.

faq.question: Can we visit the Larco Museum?
faq.answer: Yes, instead of Huaca Pucllana. It has one of the best collections of pre-Columbian art in the Americas.

faq.question: Will we be taken to shops?
faq.answer: No. There are no commission stops.

faq.question: Should we tip?
faq.answer: Tips are appreciated in Peru but never required.

faq.question: What should we wear?
faq.answer: Light layers, comfortable shoes and a jacket for the sea breeze.

faq.question: What is the best time of year?
faq.answer: December to April is sunny summer; June to September is mild and often grey with sea mist.

faq.question: What is the cancellation policy?
faq.answer: You can cancel free of charge up to 24 hours before the tour. Until your request is confirmed, nothing is charged at all.
